title: A part on an open work order can still be deactivated
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create an active tracked part, part A, for this test, with 5 in its bin.
  • Create an open work order, work order 1, for this test, with a line that holds part A, quantity 1.
  • Write down what part A's row on work order 1 shows: part number, description, quantity, price and total.
  • Start on the Inventory page, on the Active tab, with part A's part number typed in the Search box.
custom_steps:
1. Click the three-dot actions button (⋮) in the toolbar, to the left of New Inventory Part.
  2. Click Deactivate parts.
  3. Click the part A row.
  4. Click Deactivate on the dark bar.
  5. Click Deactivate in the confirmation.
  6. Click Work Orders in the top bar.
  7. Open work order 1.
  8. Click Parts in the top bar.
  9. Click Inventory in the left menu.
  10. Click the Inactive tab.
  11. Type part A's part number in the Search box.
  12. Click the clock icon (Part History) at the left of the part A row.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The menu opens.

Step 2:

  • Bulk mode turns on.

Step 3:

  • The bar reads 1 selected.

Step 4:

  • The "Deactivate parts?" confirmation opens.

Step 5:

  • The change goes through even though part A is on an open work order: a green message reads "1 part updated." and part A leaves the Active tab.

Step 6:

  • The work order list opens.

Step 7:

  • Part A is still on its line, exactly as you wrote down: same part number, description, quantity, price and total.

Step 8:

  • The Parts left menu shows Inventory.

Step 9:

  • The Inventory page opens.

Step 10:

  • The Inactive tab is selected.

Step 11:

  • Part A is listed on the Inactive tab.

Step 12:

  • Part History shows a new entry "Deactivated", with your name under Staff and today's date and time.
  • The entries that were there before are unchanged.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 33 (23 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 27 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10815 (Story 2, Deactivate Parts in Bulk), story SV-10823 (Story 10, Confirming and Recording a Status Change)

  • S2-E1: “If a part being set inactive sits on an open work order, the change still goes through.”
  • S2-E2: “That part stays on the open work order.”
  • S2-E3: “The part's work order and invoice history does not change. The status change is recorded in the part's own history (Story 10).”
  • S10-R14: “Every status change records the user who made it, and the date and time.”
  • S10-R16: “Every status change is written to the part's Part History as its own entry. A part deactivated and later reactivated keeps both entries, each with its own note.”
  • S10-R17: “The entry reads "Deactivated" or "Activated". When the user gave a note it reads "Deactivated | Reason: {note}" or "Activated | Reason: {note}". With no note it reads "Deactivated" or "Activated" and nothing more.”
